324356.title: Existence conjecture for perfect distance-dominating sets with path components
324356.statement:
Let $\Lambda_n$ be the $n$-dimensional lattice graph, and let $P_k$ denote the path on $k$ vertices. For a finite graph $H$, a $t$-PDDS$[H]$ in $\Lambda_n$ is a perfect distance-dominating set whose components are all isomorphic to $H$. The Cartesian product of graphs is denoted by $\square$.

**Existence conjecture.** Let $H$ be a finite path or a Cartesian product of two finite paths. Then a $t$-PDDS$[H]$ in $\Lambda_n$ exists if and only if at least one of the following holds: (i) $t=1$, $n\geq 2$, and $H=P_k$ for some $k\geq 1$; (ii) $t\geq 1$, $n=2$, and $H=P_k$ for some $k\geq 1$; (iii) $t\geq 1$, $n=2$, and $H=P_2\square P_k$ for some $k\geq 2$; (iv) $t=1$, $n=3r+2$ for some $r\geq 0$, and $H=P_2\square P_2$; or (v) $t=2$, $n=3$, and $H=P_2$.

This conjecture seeks to characterize the cases in which perfect distance-dominating sets with components that are paths or products of two paths exist. The source states that the authors can characterize such graphs only for $\Lambda_2$ and do not yet have enough evidence for the general case; the listed cases are proposed because they are strongly believed when $H$ has the specified form.

327891.title: Containability bound by cop number and maximum degree
327891.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\xi(G)$ for its containability number, the minimum number of cops needed to contain the robber, $c(G)$ for its cop number in the original Cops and Robbers game, and $\Delta(G)$ for its maximum degree. **Containability bound.** For every graph $G$,

$$
\xi(G)\leq \Delta(G)c(G).
$$

The paper explicitly says that the authors were unable to prove or disprove this bound; it is presented as a conjecture and remains open.

328049.title: Enumeration of minimal factors of the form $xxx^R$
328049.statement:
Let $F_m$ be the Fibonacci numbers, let $\bf r$ be the Rote-Fibonacci word, and let $(p_i)_F$, $(q_i)_F$, and $(s_i)_F$ denote the specified Fibonacci representations of the starting positions $p_i$, $q_i$, and $s_i$. Consider finite words of the form $xxx^R$ having no proper factor of the form $www^R$.

**Minimal-$xxx^R$ enumeration conjecture.** For $n=F_{3k+1}$ there are $4$ such words of length $n$. For $n=F_{3k+1}\pm F_{3k-2}$ there are $2$ such words. Otherwise there are none. For $k\geq 3$, the words are exactly the factors of $\bf r$ beginning at the positions whose Fibonacci representations are

$$
(p_1)_F=1000(010)^{k-3}001,\quad (p_2)_F=10(010)^{k-2}001,
$$

$$
(p_3)_F=1001000(010)^{k-3}001,\quad (p_4)_F=1010(010)^{k-2}001,
$$

for length $F_{3k+1}$;

$$
(q_1)_F=10(010)^{k-3}001,\quad (q_2)_F=10000(010)^{k-3}001,
$$

for length $F_{3k+1}-F_{3k-2}$; and

$$
(s_1)_F=10(010)^{k-3}001,\quad (s_2)_F=1000(01)^{k-2}001,
$$

for length $F_{3k+1}+F_{3k-2}$.

This is a detailed conjectural enumeration of the shortest, or factor-minimal, occurrences of $xxx^R$ in the Rote-Fibonacci word. It follows an explicit open problem in a section collecting claims the authors had not yet proved, so its status is open.

328427.title: Forbidden-subgraph characterization of distributive Cambrian lattices
328427.statement:
Let $W$ be a finite Coxeter group, let $gamma\in W$ be a Coxeter element, and let $Gamma_{gamma}(W)$ be the orientation of the Coxeter diagram of $W$ induced by $gamma$. Assume that $Gamma_{gamma}(W)$ does not contain any of the induced subgraphs listed in Proposition 1.6 of the source. Let $\mathcal{B}_{gamma}$ denote the corresponding $gamma$-Cambrian lattice.

**Forbidden-subgraph conjecture.** The list in Proposition 1.6 is exhaustive: if $Gamma_{gamma}(W)$ contains none of the listed induced subgraphs, then $\mathcal{B}_{gamma}$ is distributive.

This conjecture proposes a complete combinatorial criterion for distributivity of the relevant Cambrian lattices in finite Coxeter groups. The notation for $\mathcal{B}_{gamma}$ and the exact forbidden-subgraph list are given in the cited proposition.

331606.title: Saito–Woei's plateaux conjecture for graph Laplacian eigenvalues
331606.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph. A **pendant path** of $G$ is a path such that one of its end vertices has degree $1$, the other end has degree at least $3$, and all its internal vertices have degree $2$. For a positive integer $k$, let $p_k(G)$ be the number of pendant paths of length $k$ in $G$, and let $q_k(G)$ be the number of vertices of degree at least $3$ that are an end vertex of some pendant path of length $k$.

**Saito–Woei's plateaux conjecture.** For any positive integer $k$ and any graph $G$, some Laplacian eigenvalue of $G$ has multiplicity at least

$$
p_k(G)-q_k(G).
$$

The conjecture arose from the study of Laplacian eigenvalue multiplicities in dendritic trees. The source paper states that it follows from a more general result for both Laplacian and signless Laplacian eigenvalues.

332071.title: Elimination pattern conjecture for admissible colorings
332071.statement: Let $K$ be a combinatoric, let $g$ be the genus of $\abs{K}$, and let $K^\ast$ be its dual complex. An **admissible coloring** of $K^\ast$ is a coloring satisfying the condition that every two-simplex contains exactly three arrows pointing outward or corners. **Elimination pattern conjecture.** There is an admissible coloring of $K^\ast$ such that, if $g=0$, every one-simplex of $K^\ast$ has exactly one arrow, exactly six corners of $K^\ast$ are colored, and for any two adjacent zero-simplices $i$ and $j$ the colored corners can be chosen as the union of the corners of $i$ and $j$; while, if $g\geq 1$, exactly one arrow lies on all but $6g-6$ one-simplices of $K^\ast$, and no corners are colored. This coloring is intended to provide the pattern needed for the proof of the paper's main theorem; whether it exists in the stated generality is left unresolved in the supplied text.

333167.title: Conjectured permutation trinomials over finite fields of characteristic three
333167.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $q=3^k$, and let $l$ be an integer. For the first and third families, assume the stated conditions on $k$; in every family, assume the stated coprimality condition on $l$ and $q-1$. Define the following polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$:

$$
f_1(x)=x^{lq+l+5}+x^{(l+5)q+l}-x^{(l-1)q+l+6},
$$

$$
f_2(x)=x^{lq+l+1}-x^{(l+4)q+l-3}+x^{(l-2)q+l+3},
$$

$$
f_3(x)=x^{lq+l+1}+x^{(l+2)q+l-1}-x^{(l-2)q+l+3}.
$$

**Permutation trinomial conjectures.** (1) If $k$ is even and $\mathrm{gcd}(5+2l,q-1)=1$, then $f_1(x)$ is a permutation trinomial over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. (2) If $\mathrm{gcd}(1+2l,q-1)=1$, then $f_2(x)$ is a permutation trinomial over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. (3) If $\mathrm{gcd}(1+2l,q-1)=1$ and $k\not\equiv2\pmod4$, then $f_3(x)$ is a permutation trinomial over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$.

These are computer-supported conjectures proposing three parameterized families of permutation trinomials over finite fields of characteristic three. The source gives no proof or resolution, so their status remains open.

334946.title: Converse to the parking-function criterion for strongly common radical solutions
334946.statement:
Let $\mu=(\mu_1\geq\mu_2\geq\dots\geq\mu_r)$ be a partition. It admits a **strongly common radical solution** if, for some integer $m$, a common radical solution exists for any choice of $r$ distinct roots. For a permutation $\pi$ of $\mu$, write $(\pi\circ\mu)_i$ for the $i$-th entry of the resulting partition, and let $|\mu|$ denote the sum of the parts. **Converse to the parking-function criterion.** A necessary and sufficient condition for $\mu$ to admit a strongly common radical solution is that there exists a sequence $\{a_1,\ldots,a_r\}$ of positive integers such that the number of different permutations $\pi$ of $\mu$ satisfying $(\pi\circ\mu)_i\geq a_i$ is at least

$$
|\mu|-\sum_{i=1}^r a_i+2.
$$

This is presented as the converse to the sufficient condition in the preceding theorem; the source describes the claim as strongly suspected and discusses it among open problems, with only special cases currently handled.

335469.title: Bergelson–Hindman–Leader partition conjecture for the nonzero rationals
335469.statement:
Let $\mathbb{Q}\setminus\{0\}$ be partitioned into finitely many sets,

$$
\mathbb{Q}\setminus\{0\}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{r}A_i.
$$

For a sequence $\langle x_n\rangle_{n=1}^{\infty}$, let $FS(\langle x_n\rangle_{n=1}^{\infty})$ denote its finite sums and $FP(\langle x_n\rangle_{n=1}^{\infty})$ its finite products. **Bergelson–Hindman–Leader conjecture.** There exists a finite partition

$$
\mathbb{Q}\setminus\{0\}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{r}A_i
$$

such that there do not exist $i\in\{1,2,\ldots,r\}$ and a sequence $\langle x_n\rangle_{n=1}^{\infty}$ with

$$
FS(\langle x_n\rangle_{n=1}^{\infty})\cup FP(\langle x_n\rangle_{n=1}^{\infty})\subseteq A_i.
$$

This extends the corresponding result for dyadic rational numbers; the source presents it as a conjecture from Bergelson, Hindman, and Leader, and its resolution is not indicated here.

337250.title: The star characterization conjecture for graphs with one large Laplacian eigenvalue
337250.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with Laplacian eigenvalues $\mu_1\geq\cdots\geq\mu_n$ and average degree $\overline{d}(G)=2m/n$, where $m$ is the number of edges and $n$ the number of vertices. Define $\sigma(G)$ to be the number of Laplacian eigenvalues at least $\overline{d}(G)$. For integers $r\geq 1$ and $s\geq 0$, let $K_{1,r}+sK_1$ denote the disjoint union of the star $K_{1,r}$ and $s$ isolated vertices. **Star characterization conjecture.** $\sigma(G)=1$ if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $K_1$, $K_2+sK_1$ for some $s\geq 0$, or $K_{1,r}+sK_1$ for some $r\geq 2$ and $0\leq s<r-1$. The conjecture seeks a complete structural characterization of graphs having exactly one Laplacian eigenvalue at least their average degree; the paper proves it for several classes, including graphs whose complements are disconnected, but the general case remains open.

366848.title: Bodirsky–Pinsker CSP dichotomy conjecture for reducts of finitely bounded homogeneous structures
366848.statement:
Let $L$ be a finite relational language, let $\str M$ be an $L$-structure, and let a **first-order reduct** of a structure mean a structure whose relations are first-order definable in that structure. A homogeneous structure is one in which every isomorphism between finite substructures extends to an automorphism, and it is **finitely bounded** when its age is defined by forbidding finitely many finite structures. The constraint satisfaction problem $\operatorname{CSP}(\str M)$ asks, for a finite $L$-structure $\str A$, whether there is a homomorphism $\str A\to\str M$.

**Bodirsky–Pinsker conjecture.** If $\str M$ is a first-order reduct of a finitely bounded homogeneous structure in a finite relational language, then either $\operatorname{CSP}(\str M)$ is solvable in polynomial time or it is NP-complete.

This conjecture extends the finite CSP dichotomy theorem to the indicated class of infinite structures. The source says that it has been verified in several concrete instances, but remains unresolved in general.

369727.title: Cameron's fort-number lower-bound conjecture for maximum nullity
369727.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\operatorname{ft}(G)$ be its fort number, let $\operatorname{Z}^*(G)$ be its fractional zero forcing number, and let $\operatorname{M}(G)$ be its maximum nullity.

**Cameron's conjecture.** For every graph $G$,

$$
\operatorname{ft}(G)\leq \operatorname{Z}^*(G)\leq \operatorname{M}(G).
$$

The first inequality is the known general fort-number bound for fractional zero forcing. The conjecture asserts the additional lower bound on maximum nullity; it is motivated by the established inequality $\operatorname{M}(G)\leq \operatorname{Z}(G)$ and the need for lower bounds on maximum nullity.

370229.title: Brooks-type conjecture for proper conflict-free coloring
370229.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple finite undirected graph with maximum degree $Delta\geq 3$, and let $\chi_{\mathrm{pcf}}(G)$ denote its proper conflict-free chromatic number. **Brooks-type conjecture.** For every graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta\geq 3$, 

$$
\chi_{\mathrm{pcf}}(G)\leq \Delta+1.
$$

This conjecture was posed as a Brooks-type bound for proper conflict-free coloring; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

372751.title: Conjecture on the proper open conflict-free chromatic index
372751.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$, and let $\chi_{\rm pOCF}'(G)$ denote its proper open conflict-free chromatic index.

**Proper open conflict-free chromatic-index conjecture.** For every graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta$,

$$
\chi_{\rm pOCF}'(G)\leq \Delta+3.
$$

The conjecture aims to improve the currently available general upper bound, which is slightly above $2\Delta$, to within an absolute constant of the trivial lower bound $\Delta$.

375392.title: Havet–Horsch–Rambaud inversion-diameter conjecture
375392.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $I(G)$ for its inversion graph and $\operatorname{diam}(I(G))$ for its inversion diameter, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote the maximum degree of $G$.

**Havet–Horsch–Rambaud's conjecture.** For every graph $G$,

$$
\operatorname{diam}(I(G))\le \Delta(G).
$$

Havet, Horsch and Rambaud proved the weaker general bound $\operatorname{diam}(I(G))\le 2\Delta(G)-1$ and established the conjectured bound for graphs with maximum degree at most two. The conjecture is also known for several further graph classes, but its status in general is unresolved.
